reflection_question: What is the one thing you have refused to give up because it felt too extreme - and what is it actually protecting?
devotional_text:
Everything so far has been honest but gentle.

Today is not gentle, because there is a point in this where gentleness stops helping.

# What Jesus Actually Said

> "If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you." (Matthew 5:29)

> "If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you." (Matthew 5:30)

Let us deal with the obvious first. He is not telling you to injure yourself. Nobody in two thousand years of the church has read it that way, and a blind man can still lust.

It is deliberate exaggeration to make one point, and the point is this:

**Whatever is feeding this has to go, even if losing it costs you something real.**

## Why He Chose The Right Hand And Right Eye

Not a hand. The *right* hand — for most people, the good one. The useful one.

Not an eye. The *right* eye — in the ancient world, the one associated with aim and strength.

He deliberately picks the valuable thing.

Because the stuff you need to cut is never the stuff you do not care about. It is the friendship. The app that also does something useful. The job that pays well and puts you in the hotel on your own. The group that is genuinely fun until 10 p.m.

**If it was easy to lose, you would have lost it already.**

## The Part You Have Been Negotiating

You know what it is.

Through twenty-five days you have been willing to do a lot. And there is one thing you have been quietly steering around, telling yourself it is not really the problem, or that getting rid of it would be an overreaction.

That is usually the thing.

Write down what came to mind just now. Do not argue with the first answer.

## "More Profitable For You"

Notice the reasoning Jesus gives.

> "For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna." (Matthew 5:29)

**More profitable for you.**

This is not God taking something away because He disapproves of your enjoyment. It is arithmetic. He is saying: do the sum. Compare what you lose with what it is costing.

You have been treating the cut as pure loss. He frames it as the better of two trades.

## What This Looks Like Now

For somebody in this fight, in 2026, the hand and the eye usually mean:

* 📱 The device, or the app, or the account — gone, not "managed"
* 👥 The friendship that only exists around the thing
* 💳 The card, the account, the easy access to money
* 🛣️ The route, the shop, the part of town
* 🏠 The arrangement — the night alone every week, the trip, the late shift
* 📺 The subscription that is ninety percent fine and ten percent the problem

The test is not whether it is mostly harmless. The test is whether it *causes you to stumble*.

## The Half Measure Problem

Half measures feel wise. They are usually just slower surrender.

*I will keep it but set a limit. I will keep the friendship but not go to those places. I will install the filter but keep the password.*

Everybody in this fight has run those experiments. They work until a bad week.

**An addiction does not need a door. It needs a crack.**

## One Honest Warning

Cutting something off is not the same as being free, and if you treat it as the whole answer you will be disappointed.

Removing access buys you time and lowers the pressure. It does not deal with the thirst underneath — that was Day 4, and days 31 to 40 are about what replaces it.

But you cannot do the deeper work while the thing is still within arm's reach. **Cut first, build second.**

## What To Watch For In Matthew 5:27-30

* 👁️ Where Jesus locates the problem in verse 28 — before any action
* 🤚 That He picks the *right* hand and *right* eye
* 🧮 The phrase "more profitable for you"
* 🔥 How serious He treats this, in a sermon otherwise full of mercy
* ⚖️ That He offers a comparison, not a condemnation

## The Bigger Takeaway

There is something you have been protecting.

You have reasons, and the reasons are good, and that is exactly why it has survived this long.

**Jesus is not asking you to be reasonable. He is asking you to be free.**

## Today's One Thing

**Cut one thing, today, properly.**

Not "from Monday." Not "I will cut down." Today, and completely.

And make it irreversible by yourself:

* 🔑 Somebody else holds the password, and you do not know it
* 📵 The app is deleted and the account is closed, not just logged out
* 💳 The card is cancelled, not hidden
* 🗣️ The arrangement is told to somebody who will notice if it comes back

If you can undo it alone at midnight, you have not cut it. You have moved it.

This will feel like too much. That feeling is the point of the verse.

## Today's Prayer

Jesus,

I know what it is. I have known the whole way through this study and I have been steering around it.

I have good reasons for keeping it. I have been rehearsing them for years.

But You said the hand and the eye, and You meant the useful ones, and I am not going to pretend I do not understand You.

Give me the nerve to do it today, not Monday.

And be honest with me — take anything else I am still negotiating about, even if I cannot see it yet.

I would rather lose it than keep living like this.

In Your name, amen.

reflection_question: Who have you hurt or taken from? What is one thing you could actually put right this month?
devotional_text:
There is a part of this nobody enjoys talking about.

You have not only damaged yourself. There is money that was not yours. Promises broken. People lied to. Things taken.

Twenty-six days in, with the honesty you have built, it is time.

# A Man Everybody Hated

Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector. In first-century Jericho that meant he worked for the occupying empire and made his money by charging his own people more than Rome required and keeping the difference.

Rich, and despised, and both because of the same thing.

He climbs a tree to see Jesus, because he is short and the crowd will not let him through. Grown men do not climb trees. He wanted to see badly enough not to care.

## What Jesus Does

> "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house." (Luke 19:5)

He uses his name. Again — like Hagar.

And He invites Himself to dinner, publicly, in front of a town that had spent years agreeing that this man was beyond the pale.

> "When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, 'He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.'" (Luke 19:7)

Jesus goes in first. Before any apology, before any repayment, before Zacchaeus has said a single word about changing.

**Grace is not the reward for putting things right. It is what makes putting things right possible.**

## And Then Zacchaeus Stands Up

Nobody asked him to.

> "Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much." (Luke 19:8)

Four times.

The law required a fifth added on top in some cases of restitution. Four times was the penalty for stealing and slaughtering somebody's ox — the harshest category.

He did not look for the minimum. He went past it, voluntarily, out of a joy that had arrived about twenty minutes earlier.

That is what real repentance produces. Not a negotiation about the least you can get away with.

## What This Means For You

There is a list. You know roughly who is on it.

* 💷 Money borrowed with a story attached
* 🧾 Money taken quietly from somebody who has not noticed, or has and said nothing
* 🤥 A lie somebody is still living with as though it were true
* 🎂 The thing you missed, and the reason you gave
* 💔 A person who thinks the problem was them

Making it right is part of turning. It is not optional, and it is not penance either — notice that Zacchaeus did it *after* salvation came to his house, not to buy it.

## Four Honest Cautions

This is the day where people do damage with good intentions, so read these.

1. **Do not confess to somebody to relieve yourself at their expense.** If telling them helps you and devastates them for no good reason, that is not amends. That is offloading. This matters most with betrayals a person does not know about — get wise counsel first, from somebody who is not involved.
2. **Do not make promises instead of payments.** A person who has heard ten promises does not need an eleventh. They need twenty pounds and a changed Tuesday.
3. **Some things cannot be repaid.** Time, a childhood, a marriage. For those, the amends is who you become from here, over years, without being asked.
4. **Do not do this while still using, if it means exposing somebody else to more harm.** Stabilise first where you need to.

## And Where It Lands

> "For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost." (Luke 19:10)

That is the sentence at the end of the Zacchaeus story.

**Came to seek.** He did not wait at the gate of Jericho for the respectable people to come out. He walked in and looked up a tree.

## What To Watch For In Luke 19:1-10

* 🌳 What Zacchaeus is willing to look ridiculous for
* 👀 Who sees whom first, in verse 5
* 🏠 That Jesus goes in before anything has been put right
* 🗣️ That the crowd's objection is correct — he *is* a sinner
* 4️⃣ That Zacchaeus chooses four times, which nobody demanded
* 🔍 The last verse, and the word "seek"

## The Bigger Takeaway

You cannot build a clean life on top of a debt you are pretending is not there.

Some of what you owe is money. Most of it is truth.

**Zacchaeus did not pay people back in order to be accepted. He had already been accepted, and that is precisely why he could afford to be honest about what he had taken.**

## Today's One Thing

**Make the list. Then do the smallest one.**

Two columns.

* **Who** — the person
* **What** — money, a lie, an absence, a promise

Write everyone you can think of, even the ones you cannot face yet. The list being long is not a verdict on you; it is what this does to a life.

Then pick the **smallest, most doable one** and complete it this week. Not the biggest. The smallest.

Twenty pounds returned. One text saying "I was not honest with you about that, and I am sorry."

Amends is a muscle. You build it on the small ones first.

## Today's Prayer

Jesus,

I have taken things.

Money, trust, time, truth. From people who did not deserve it, and some of them still do not know.

I have avoided this part because once I look at the list I will have to do something about it, and some of it frightens me.

You went into the house of a man who had robbed an entire town, before he offered to pay a penny back.

So do that here, and then give me what You gave him — the kind of freedom where putting it right stops feeling like a punishment and starts feeling like relief.

Show me where to begin. Give me wisdom about what would heal and what would only hurt somebody else.

And make me somebody whose word means something again.

In Your name, amen.

day_title: Say It To A Human Being
reflection_question: What is actually stopping you telling the person whose name you wrote on Day 3?
devotional_text:
On Day 3 you wrote down a name.

It has been twenty-five days. For most people reading this, nothing has happened with it.

Today we deal with that.

# The Verse

> "Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed." (James 5:16)

Two things to notice before anything else.

**"To one another."** Not only to God. To a person, out loud, who can hear it and respond.

**"That you may be healed."** There is a result attached. James links confession to another human being with healing — not with humiliation, not with punishment.

## Why A Person And Not Just God

Telling God is essential and it is not sufficient, and here is the honest reason why.

When you confess only to God, **nothing in the visible world changes.** No one looks at you differently. No one asks you about it next week. You can confess on Sunday and be back in it on Wednesday with no friction at all.

A person introduces friction.

And there is something else. Shame tells you that if anyone knew the real thing, they would be finished with you. That belief can only be *disproved* by somebody actually knowing and not being finished with you.

God knowing does not disprove it, because a quiet voice inside says *yes, but He has to love me, that is His job.*

**You need one human being to know and stay.** That is where the healing in this verse lives.

## What It Does To The Thing Itself

Addiction is strongest in the dark. That is not a metaphor.

The whole structure depends on compartments — the version at work, the version at church, the version at home, and none of them talking to each other.

One person who knows the truth collapses the compartments. Suddenly there is somewhere the real thing is already known, and the energy you were spending on maintenance comes back to you.

## The Passage Around It

James does not drop this verse in isolation. Look what surrounds it.

> "Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises. Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly." (James 5:13-14)

**Let him call.** The sick person initiates. Nobody comes and finds them.

That is the uncomfortable part. Nobody is going to guess. You have been too good at hiding for anybody to guess.

And then at the very end of the letter:

> "He who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death, and will cover a multitude of sins." (James 5:20)

The person you tell is not being burdened. They are being given something to do that James calls saving a soul from death.

You may have been protecting them from a weight they would consider an honour.

## How To Actually Do It

People do not fail at this because they lack courage. They fail because they have no script. So here is one.

**Pick the moment.** Not after a relapse at 1 a.m. Somewhere neutral, sober, with time.

**Open with what you are asking for.** "I need to tell you something, and I am not asking you to fix it. I just need one person to know."

**Say the real thing.** The actual word. Not "I have been struggling."

**Say how long.** The length is usually the part you most want to shave down. Do not.

**Say what you want from them.** "Can I text you when it is bad?" "Will you ask me about it every Sunday?" Be specific, or it evaporates in a week.

## If It Goes Badly

It might. People react out of their own fear, and some first reactions are poor.

A bad reaction from one person is not a verdict on the whole idea. It means you picked wrong, or caught them wrong.

And if there is genuinely nobody in your life — that is not the end of the road either. **A doctor, a counsellor, or a recovery group exists precisely for this.** A room full of strangers who will not flinch is worth more than a close friend who cannot cope, and there is no shame in starting there.

## What To Watch For In James 5:13-20

* 📞 Who does the calling in verse 14
* 🤝 "To one another" in verse 16 — both directions
* 💊 That healing is the stated purpose
* 💪 "The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective"
* 🧍 Elijah in verses 17 and 18, described as "a man with a nature like ours"
* 🫂 What verse 20 says about the person who helps somebody turn

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have carried this alone because you believed that was the responsible thing, or the only safe thing.

It has not worked, and Scripture does not ask it of you.

**Confess to one another, that you may be healed.** The healing is attached to the telling.

## Today's One Thing

**Send the message.**

Not the confession. The message that makes the conversation happen.

To the name from Day 3. Something like:

*"Can I talk to you about something properly this week? Not on text. It is nothing you have done."*

That is it. One message, today.

If the name is blank, make the other call instead: a doctor's appointment, a counsellor, or find the time and place of one local recovery meeting and write it in your calendar.

**Twenty-five days ago you wrote a name down. Today it stops being a name on paper.**

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have been doing this on my own because telling somebody felt like the end of my life as I know it.

I am starting to see that the life I am protecting is not much of a life.

Your word says confess to one another and be healed. It does not say be humiliated. It says healed.

Give me the courage to send one message today.

And go ahead of me — prepare whoever it is. Give them the right words. Let them be steady.

I am so tired of being the only one who knows.

In Jesus' name, amen.

day_title: The Narrow Road Is Still A Road
reflection_question: What have you been telling yourself about how hard the road out of this is? Is that assessment honest, or is it an excuse?
devotional_text:
Two verses today. They are short and they are honest, and the honesty is why they help.

# What Jesus Says

> "Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it. How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it." (Matthew 7:13-14)

Two roads. Two gates.

One is wide. One is narrow and the word is **restricted** — cramped, pressed, hard going.

And Jesus does not sell it. He does not tell you the narrow road is secretly the easy one once you get going. He says it is narrow and restricted, and most people do not take it.

## Why That Honesty Helps

Because you have been lied to by encouragement.

Somebody has told you that if you just give it to God it lifts. That one prayer, one altar call, one decision and it is done.

And for a small number of people something like that does happen. For most it does not, and when it did not happen to you, you concluded that your faith was defective.

**Jesus says the road is hard.** If it is hard for you, you are on the right road, not the wrong one.

That single reframe has kept more people going than any amount of cheerfulness.

## The Wide Road Is Wide For A Reason

The wide gate is easy to go through. That is its entire appeal.

No cutting anything off. No conversation with the person from Day 3. No list of amends. Nothing to turn around today. You simply keep doing what you are doing and let it carry you.

And it is **broad** — there is room on it. Lots of company. Plenty of people to agree with you that this is normal, that everybody has something, that you are fine.

The wide road is not where defiant people go. It is where people go who did not decide anything.

## "Few Are Those Who Find It"

That line can land as discouraging. Read it the other way.

It means **the road exists.** Some find it. It is not theoretical.

There are people alive today who were exactly where you are and are now years clear. Not because they were stronger than you. Because they found a narrow gate and went through it and kept walking when it was cramped.

## What Narrow Actually Means Day To Day

It is worth being concrete, because "narrow" sounds spiritual and is usually extremely practical.

* 🚪 Fewer options. You cannot go everywhere everyone else goes, for a while.
* ⏰ More structure. The hour from Day 5 has to have a plan in it.
* 👥 Fewer secrets. Somebody knows, and that is permanent now.
* 🐢 Slower. Nothing dramatic happens for weeks at a time.
* 🔁 Repetitive. The same choice, made again, on a Tuesday nobody is watching.

Narrow does not mean miserable. It means **fewer ways to go**, which is exactly what somebody in your position needs.

## The Verse Right After

Keep reading past verse 14 and Jesus immediately warns about false prophets, "in sheep's clothing."

That is not a change of subject. People will offer you a wider version of the narrow road. A shortcut. A way to keep one thing. A teaching where nothing actually has to be cut off.

Be careful of anybody who makes this sound simple. Jesus did not.

## What To Watch For In Matthew 7:13-14

* 🚪 That there are two gates and two ways, and everyone is on one of them
* 📏 The words "narrow" and "restricted"
* 👥 Who is on the broad road — "many"
* 🎯 That the narrow one leads to *life*, not merely to safety
* 🔎 "Few are those who find it" — find implies looking

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been measuring your progress against a promise nobody in Scripture made you.

The road out of this is narrow and cramped and slow, and Jesus said so plainly before you ever set foot on it.

**The difficulty is not evidence that it is not working. It is the terrain.**

## Today's One Thing

**Write down the hardest part of the next thirty days, and decide now how you will handle it.**

Be specific. Not "temptation." The actual thing:

* The Friday when everyone goes out
* The first night in the house alone after the cut on Day 26
* Telling the person on Day 28 and then having to live with them knowing
* The week your usual reason to use comes round again

Name it. Then write one sentence about what you will do when it arrives.

You are not making it easier. You are refusing to be ambushed by something you could see coming.

**Narrow is survivable when you know it is narrow.**

## Today's Prayer

Jesus,

Thank You for not pretending.

Everybody else has told me this would be simple if I believed hard enough, and then I failed and thought the problem was my faith.

You said the road is narrow and restricted and that most people do not take it. That is the first thing anybody has said about this that matched my experience.

I am on the hard road. Help me stop treating the hardness as proof that I am failing.

Give me what I need for the cramped parts. Keep me walking on the days when nothing happens and nothing changes.

And thank You that it leads to life. Not just away from something. Toward something.

In Your name, amen.

reflection_question: Halfway. What is the one choice in front of you today - not this year, today?
devotional_text:
Halfway.

Thirty days ago you said the real name of it out loud. Since then: the lie, the secret, the thirst, the cost, the outside view, the morning after, the God who sees, the God who does not condemn, the broom tree, the charcoal fire, the turning, the cutting, the list, the message.

Some of you have thirty clean days. Some of you have had a terrible fortnight.

**Both of you are halfway through, and that is not nothing.**

Today is a hinge. Moses at the end of his life, speaking to a nation about to go somewhere he will not.

# First, He Removes An Excuse

> "For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant." (Deuteronomy 30:11)

**Not too hard for you.**

He says it before anything else, because he knows what they are about to say. *We cannot. It is beyond us.*

And then he makes it very concrete:

> "It is not in heaven, that you should say, 'Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us?' Neither is it beyond the sea." (Deuteronomy 30:12-13)

You do not have to send somebody to heaven for it. You do not have to cross an ocean.

> "But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it." (Deuteronomy 30:14)

**Very near to you.**

The thing you need is not somewhere exotic. It is not in a retreat you cannot afford or a breakthrough you have not had yet. It is close enough to act on this morning.

## Then The Choice

> "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants." (Deuteronomy 30:19)

Three things in that verse worth sitting with.

**"Today."** Not in general. Not for the rest of your life. Today.

**"Choose life."** It is an imperative. Somebody has to actually choose. God sets the options out; He does not pick for you.

**"You and your descendants."** This does not stop with you. That is heavy and it is true. The way you handle this shapes what your children think is normal, what they inherit, and what they have to fight.

## Why "Today" Is The Key Word

One of the reasons people fail at this is that they try to choose for *years* at once.

*Never again. For the rest of my life. No more, ever.*

That is an enormous commitment to make on a Tuesday with a headache, and the size of it is paralysing. So you fail at it, and then you fail at the whole thing, because the whole thing was staked on a promise no human being can feel their way into keeping.

Moses says *today*.

Recovery communities have said the same thing for a century, in three words: **just for today.** It is in Deuteronomy first.

You are not being asked to choose life for the next thirty years. You are being asked to choose it before bed.

## What The Second Half Holds

* 🧱 **Days 31-40. Rebuilding.** Your hours, your body, your triggers, your people. The practical half.
* 🩹 **Days 41-50. When you fall.** Because some will, and what you do in the next hour decides whether it is a fall or a return.
* 🌅 **Days 51-60. A life bigger than this.** What all of it is actually for.

The first thirty days were about truth and about God. The next thirty are about building a life that does not need the thing.

## What To Watch For In Deuteronomy 30:11-20

* 🚫 The excuse Moses removes in verse 11, before they can use it
* 🌊 How far away it is *not*, in verses 12 and 13
* 👄 "In your mouth and in your heart" — how close it is
* ⚖️ The two options in verse 19, named plainly
* 📅 How many times "today" appears
* 👨‍👩‍👧 "You and your descendants"

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been trying to make one enormous choice that covers the rest of your life, and collapsing under the weight of it.

Moses puts it in front of a whole nation and shrinks it to one word: **today.**

Thirty days from now there will have been thirty todays. That is the only way anybody has ever done this.

## Today's One Thing

**Choose life, out loud, for today only.**

Say it in your own words, with the date in it.

*"Today, the twenty-fourth, I choose life. Not forever. Today."*

Then write down the **one** choice that stands between you and the end of this day. Just one. The specific fork you know is coming.

And before you close this, go back to Day 20 and read what you wrote about what had changed.

You are halfway. Keep walking.

## Today's Prayer

God,

Thirty days.

I thought I would be further along. Some of it has gone well and some of it has not, and You have seen all of it.

I have been trying to promise You forever, and I cannot. Forever is too big and I break it by Thursday.

So today. Just today.

Today I choose life. Today I choose You over the thing that has been taking my life a piece at a time.

And if there are people after me — kids, a family, anybody watching — let this be where it stops being handed on.

Help me do thirty more todays.

In Jesus' name, amen.
